findings.title: Upsampled count ignores NULL sample_weight, so events without a sample rate count as 0
findings.body: `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()`, which is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. Only events that carry a client sample rate get a `sample_weight`. Events in allowlisted projects that predate rollout, or come from SDKs that don't send `client_sample_rate`, have NULL there. `sum` skips NULLs, so those events add 0 and the chart undercounts, possibly showing 0 for projects that do have errors. The comments ("rely on the database schema to ensure sample_weight exists") assert a guarantee nothing in the PR enforces. The aggregate should treat missing weights as 1, for example `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))`.

findings.title: Eligibility cache is stale for 60s and its invalidation function is never called
findings.body: The result of the allowlist check is cached for 60s under a key built only from org id and project ids, not from the allowlist contents. After an operator changes `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, queries keep using the old decision for up to a minute. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is documented as the fix but has no callers, so it is dead code. The `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` docstring says the config is read "fresh each time" to have the latest state, which contradicts the cache. The key also uses `hash(tuple(...))`, so two project sets can collide and get each other's cached answer; joining the sorted ids would be collision-free.

findings.title: The "performance" cache adds a cache round trip for something that is already cheap
findings.body: `options.get` is served from Sentry's local option cache, and the allowlist check is a few integer lookups. Wrapping it in `cache.get`/`cache.set` adds a network round trip (memcached/redis) on every `_get_event_stats` call, and the dashboard split path calls that function several times per request. The dataset and query check, which is the cheap part, runs after the cache access, so even spans, transactions and metrics requests pay for the lookup. The cache costs more than it saves. Evaluating `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` first and dropping the cache would be simpler and faster.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses the outer `dataset` and the raw request query, not the dataset and query actually being executed
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but the eligibility check passes the closure variable `dataset` and `_is_error_focused_query` re-reads `request.GET['query']`. In the dashboard-widget split flow the function is called with `discover` and a derived query such as `(q) AND !event.type:transaction`, and also with the original dataset and query. The decision then reflects neither the dataset nor the query of the call being made. Error-only split queries are not upsampled unless the user's raw query happens to contain `event.type:error`. A transactions or metrics query can be judged eligible because of the outer dataset. The decision should be based on `scoped_dataset` and the `query` argument.

findings.title: Substring match on `event.type:error` misclassifies queries
findings.body: `"event.type:error" in query` is a raw substring test on the lowercased query string. It is also true for `!event.type:error` (errors excluded), for `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` (transactions have no `sample_weight`), and for values like `event.type:error_foo`. Those queries get `count()` rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)`, producing wrong numbers or failing on transaction rows. Parse the query, or at least check for the negation and OR cases.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` is a public discover function not restricted to error data
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered without `private=True`, so any caller of the events or stats API can request `upsampled_count()` directly. On transactions, spans or any non-error query this references a `sample_weight` column that does not exist, so users get Snuba errors or a 500 instead of a validation error. It is also not gated on the allowlist. The function is an internal rewrite target and should be private, like the neighbouring internal function.

findings.title: Comments claim caching, separation and "current schema assumptions" that the code does not implement
findings.body: The comments say "This cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution", "This separation allows for better query optimization and caching" and "ensure we use the most current schema assumptions". The check runs on every call, `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` is a pure alias, and the "late transformation" is just a list rewrite. The same transform block is also copy-pasted into three branches. The comments mislead readers about the behavior and should be removed, and the transform done once.

findings.title: No tests for the eligibility entry point, the cache, or invalidation
findings.body: The unit tests cover only the private helpers. `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, the cache hit/miss paths and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` are never exercised, and nothing checks that an allowlist change is picked up. Negated or OR-combined `event.type` queries and the topEvents path are not tested either. The `snuba_params` built in `setUp` is never used. The endpoint tests mock `options` but not the cache, so they depend on cache state between runs.

findings.title: Stray submodule gitlink committed
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` entry as a gitlink (`Subproject commit a5d29095...`, the base commit of this very repo) with no matching `.gitmodules`. It is unrelated to the feature and almost certainly an accident. It leaves a dangling submodule entry that makes `git submodule` commands error and confuses checkouts and CI. It should be removed from the PR.
